column3: question
Is BinaryFormatter output persisted (database, files, session, cache) and needed after migration?
Who consumes these WCF services (internal apps, partners) and which bindings/security modes do they use?
Which external systems call these SOAP endpoints, and can they change contract?
Which identity provider tenant/app registrations does each application use, and who can add the new redirect URIs?
How are desktop clients deployed and updated (MSI, ClickOnce, manual), and how many are installed?
Which time zone are the current servers set to, and which business rules depend on it?
Where are production connection strings configured (IIS, transforms, deployment tool), and do they use Windows or SQL authentication?

Server inventory per application: OS version, CPU/RAM, IIS version and modules, app-pool identities, and current utilisation (for right-sizing).
Hypervisor and network: VMware / Hyper-V / Proxmox version, static IPs, VLANs and firewall rules the applications rely on.
Scheduled tasks, Windows services and SQL Agent jobs running on the servers (the repositories rarely contain all of them).
Certificates in use (TLS, client, signing) and where their private keys live.
Compliance regime (HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOC 2, ISO 27001) and data-residency constraints that limit AWS Regions or services.
How users authenticate today (AD, ADFS, Entra ID, local accounts) and whether a move to SSO/OIDC is acceptable.
Database sizes, growth, maintenance windows and acceptable downtime for cut-over.
Partners that allow-list our source IPs, VPN tunnels and on-prem systems that stay on-premises.
Branching model, release cadence, and whether a code-freeze window per wave is possible.
Availability of QA with domain knowledge, test environments and test data per wave.
Current Windows Server and SQL Server licences (edition, cores, Software Assurance / licence mobility) for the cost model (AWS OLA).
